description: `from unittest import skipIf as print` shadows the builtin `print`, which Python falls back to wherever the module's own binding is not yet made (a use before the import). A name that is also a builtin is not certainly the import at every occurrence, so `@print(True, "x")` is a WARN (it may skip), not a FAIL (round 5: the rule is about the whole file). The real runner skips the test.
